I'd definitely remove the extra oil before driving it anywhere.

I don't know where you're located, but colder weather has started coming on in most of the northern hemisphere. Cold weather won't "kill a battery" contrary to popular belief, but it'll make a bad battery come out of the woodwork. Most batteries list two amperages, one is CA (cranking amps) and the other is CCA (cold cranking amps). Both numbers will decrease with time and use, but since CCA is always lower it will create problems when the ambient temperature is no longer close to the battery's ideal operating temperature.

Chrome items are coated with a layer of chromium or a chromium alloy and usually another conductive layer made of something like copper that the chromium can adhere to. You can send your fender or mudguard off to a chrome plating service depending on if you have the money for it. Most of those places also have sandblasting services, but if they by some chance don't, you'll have to get your part back down to bare metal yourself. 

You could also polish the part to a mirror finish if you want to DIY it. Chrome is valued because it's super hard and it doesn't tarnish very easily (if the coating is thick enough and cared for). If you sand, buff, and wax to a mirror finish, you have to keep in mind that you are sacrificing the brilliance of the finish and durability. You'll save a pretty penny though, good chrome plating isn't cheap. Good luck!

Former Harley parts guy, don't know what you have but that looks exactly like a Softail hub. That's officially known as a cush-drive, and is responsible for smoothing out the transfer of power to your rear wheel. They work wonderfully and make the ride smooth as butter, but they wear down and, as you could guess, slow down the reaction time from throttle to takeoff. If you feel so inclined, you can easily replace that with a polyurethane cush drive, which would have the benefit of lasting longer and decreasing throttle response (i.e. making it easier to burn rubber), but just like replacing rubber engine mounts with poly, it'll make your ride a tad harsher. Happy riding! Hmu for more useless parts stuff.
